summary: TechCrunch reports that Epic Games is returning Fortnite to its original Chapter 1 map on November 3, 2023, while keeping some modern mobility perks, as part of a broader gaming nostalgia trend. The article compares this to World of Warcraft Classic and cites hits like Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, Super Mario Bros. Wonder and the Final Fantasy VII remake. Blizzard Watch's Elizabeth Harper explains why nostalgia sells and why classic re-releases need some modern conveniences.
one_line: Epic Games brings Fortnite back to its original Chapter 1 map on November 3, 2023, reflecting gaming's wider nostalgia boom and World of Warcraft Classic's precedent.
key_facts: Epic Games announced on Friday (October 27, 2023) that Fortnite's next season would return to its original Chapter 1 map, starting November 3, 2023.
Epic hinted that modern mobility features like sprinting and mantling (a parkour-like climbing move) would remain in the retro version.
Ninja (Tyler Blevins) promoted the relaunch by showing a giant replica of a Durr Burger in his backyard, and other classic Fortnite streamers got similar treatment.
Fortnite is a battle royale third-person shooter in which 100 players compete on a shrinking island to be the last one standing.
Fortnite launched in 2017, and in 2020 it had more registered players than the population of the United States, though Epic keeps its metrics private.
Fortnite releases new content roughly every three months, with events like an Ariana Grande concert, a Darth Vader lightsaber fight and Goku as a skin.
Fortnite now competes with free-to-play rivals such as Apex Legends and Call of Duty: Warzone.
The Zelda game Tears of the Kingdom built a new game on top of the old one, and Nintendo released Super Mario Bros. Wonder, the first 2D side-scrolling Mario game in more than a decade.
Square Enix's remake of the 1997 game Final Fantasy VII is split into three standalone full-length games spaced a few years apart.
Blizzard Entertainment launched World of Warcraft Classic in 2019, reluctantly according to Elizabeth Harper, responding to community demand after third parties ran their own 'classic' servers.
Harper said the WoW Classic team initially wanted no changes but now feels some changes are needed; she described modern World of Warcraft as 'a ship of Theseus'.
World of Warcraft Classic recreated a 15-year-old version of the game, while Fortnite's throwback targets a much more recent era.
